title: Make the ground pad solderable
story: This is a thermal circuit, not an electrical one: voltage stands for temperature above the 25 C room, current for heat flow in watts, resistance for thermal resistance in K/W and capacitance for heat capacity in J/K. A 350 C soldering iron (325 above room) touches a ground pad through 15 K/W of contact. The joint itself holds 0.02 J/K. The pad joins a big ground plane (3 J/K, losing heat to the room through 10 K/W) through slot S1: a solid connection (2 K/W), a wide four-spoke thermal relief (8 K/W) or a thin four-spoke thermal relief (25 K/W). SAC305 solder melts at 217 C, which is 192 above room. The joint must melt within 3 seconds.

goals.label: the joint reaches 217 C within 3 s

hints: While the plane is still cold, the joint sits on a divider: 325 * R_link / (15 + R_link).
The plane slowly warms, but its 3 J/K takes many seconds to heat up.
